ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle with B as the center. M, B, Q are on the same horizontal straight line, BM and BQ are opposite rays; L, B, P are on the same slanted line, BL points toward the upper left, BP points toward the lower right, and they are opposite rays. The problem gives m∠LBM = 3x, m∠LBQ = 4x + 61. Reasoning: Because BM and BQ are opposite rays, ∠LBM and ∠LBQ form a linear pair, and their sum is 180°. Therefore 3x + (4x + 61) = 180, giving 7x + 61 = 180, 7x = 119, x = 17. Thus m∠LBQ = 4(17) + 61 = 129°. Also because BL and BP are opposite rays, ∠LBQ and ∠PBQ are supplementary, therefore m∠PBQ = 180° - 129° = 51°.

method.method_draft: From the image, read that M, B, and Q lie on one straight horizontal diameter, with ray BL between BM and BQ in the upper-left direction, and ray BP is the continuation of BL through B toward the lower right. From the text, use m∠LBM = 3x and m∠LBQ = 4x + 61. Since BM and BQ are opposite rays, ∠LBM and ∠LBQ form a linear pair, so 3x + (4x + 61) = 180. Solve x = 17, so m∠LBQ = 129.
